To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bacterial response to petroleum pollution is characterized by the immediate expression of RHD gene in a specific strain of Pseudomonas, and the RHD expression correlates with high biodegradative levels of low molecular weight PAHA.
ring-hydroxidation dioxygenases are expressed during the early response of the bacterial community of a chronically petroleum polluted environment to petroleum contamination.

the bacterial community from the sediment of a chronically contaminated site is ready to respond to a sudden oil input, and that the expression of the RHO gene is correlated with biodegradation levels of low molecular weight PAHS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first response of a bacterial population in the presence of a hydrocarbon pollutant.
the early functional response of an oil-polluted sediment microbial community to petroleum contamination and the expression of key genes involved in the hydrocarbon degradation.
the early functional response of the microbial community from the chronically oil-polylluted sediments of the Etang de berre (France) to the petroleum addition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
monitoring the expression of RHO genes, key genes of the hydrocarbon degradation, could provide useful information for the management of the bioremediation process.
the expression of the genes of interest was correlated with high levels of degradation of low molecular weight PAHS at 7 day of incubation.
monitoring of the expression of RRD genes in response to petroleum addition may be used to predict the efficiency of bioremediation strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monitoring the expression of RHO genes, key genes in hydrocarbon degradation could be useful in managing bioremediations.
the expression of the RHO gene was correlated with the biodegradation of the low molecular weight PAHS and the expression of this gene is specific and immediate after the petroleum contamination.
the RHD expression was a key step in the biodegradation of petroleum hydrocarbons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monitoring the expression of key genes involved in biodegradation may provide information for managing biodegradation processes.
the expression of RHO genes was only observed for a few hours after oil contamination, and that the RHO gene diversity was maintained during the whole incubation period.
monitoring the expression of RHO genes, key genes in hydrocarbon degradation processes, may provide useful and relevant information to manage bioremediation.
